ledger.claim: The rider's cleanest route to a refund — a waiting-period shortfall under POL-NS-06 — is closed on this record, and the rider does not seek a refund on that ground: the minimum in force for this trip is the 180 s free waiting period carried in trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, while the derived effective in-geofence dwell is a single continuous run of 436 s made up of 45 in-radius fixes from 21:26:22 to 21:33:38 — a surplus of 256 s, not a shortfall. The cancellation came 437 s after the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix, so nothing in POL-NS-06 refunds the $4.50.

The rider also does not allege a false arrival marker under POL-NS-05, because the derived arrival facts foreclose it: the dwell start offset from the driver's 21:26:22 'I'm Here' event is 0.0 s, so the first qualifying in-geofence fix and the arrival marker coincide and the driver cannot have been more than the arrival radius off the pin at the marker; a recomputed waiting clock under POL-NS-05 would begin at the identical fix and the corrected dwell would still be 436 s, which satisfies POL-NS-05(iii) rather than defeating the fee, leaving the outcome on POL-NS-01.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider and is not pressed: limb (a) requires a message sent by the rider during the waiting window, and the chat log contains exactly one message, which is the driver's ('im at the pickup point', sent 21:26:42, delivered 21:26:43, read 21:27:12), so there is no unanswered rider contact for the judge to weigh; and limb (c) fails on its own arithmetic in any event, because the rider's track contains 0 qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius — its fixes sit roughly 798 m to 805 m from the pin for the whole window — so the rider cannot show presence at the pickup point.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup point, and the absence is itself citable: EV-ADVIS-02728-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, and has weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. The consequence for this case is that POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable to the driver — there is no advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT that would permit separate in-geofence intervals to be summed, and no lawful-holding excuse — so the driver's position-holding must stand or fall on that single 436 s in-geofence interval, unaggregated and unexcused, and no part of the dwell may be supplemented by a document that does not exist.

The rider's own location is not an element of the charge and should not be treated as one: POL-NS-01 limb (d) tests the absence of a boarding event, the driver's cancellation_reason_code and the time of termination against the elapsed dwell — not where the rider's device was — and the only clause in this category that tests rider position at all, POL-NS-04(c), is a clause a rider invokes to be exonerated, not a condition of the fee. The rider likewise accepts that the driver made a single in-app message and no voice call (trip_record.in_app_calls is empty), and notes only that no clause conditions the fee on any further contact attempt, so that fact is neutral rather than an admission. The rider asks the judge to decide the fee on the driver's documented arrival and dwell and to record the rider's distance from the pin as context, not as a separate adverse finding about the rider's conduct.
The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for this trip: 'Driver tapped I'm Here' at 2026-08-18T21:26:22+08:00, which satisfies limb (a) of POL-NS-01 on the face of the record.

Limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is met on the GPS trace: the driver's longest qualifying run inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius begins at 2026-08-18T21:26:22+08:00 — the exact timestamp of the arrival event — so the driver was inside the pickup geofence at or before that event. The run contains 45 qualifying fixes and the driver's minimum recorded distance from the pin is 0.11 m, far inside the radius.

Limb (c) of POL-NS-01 is met with a wide margin: the driver held position inside the geofence for a continuous 436 seconds — 45 qualifying fixes from 21:26:22 to 21:33:38 — against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec. The dwell does not need to be reconstructed from the arrival tap, because it is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and here the two coincide.

Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 is met: the trip record shows no boarding event, and the trip was terminated by the driver at 21:33:39 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one second after the 436 second in-geofence dwell completed at 21:33:38, and 436 seconds after that dwell began. The cancellation therefore falls after the required dwell elapsed and under a reason code POL-NS-01(d) recognises.

The false-arrival check in POL-NS-05 does not bite on this trip. The arrival marker carries a dwell_start_offset_sec of 0.0, meaning the first qualifying in-geofence fix is contemporaneous with the 'arrived' tap, so the marker neither post-dates the geofence entry nor depends on a recomputed clock. Even if the marker were treated as false, POL-NS-05(iii) preserves the fee where the corrected dwell still meets the minimum — and 436 seconds does.

No waiting-period shortfall exists under POL-NS-06: the measured in-geofence dwell exceeds the 180 second minimum by 256 seconds (shortfall_sec = -256.0), so the cancellation fee is chargeable and no refund route in that clause opens.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider on this record. Limb (a) fails because the chat log contains exactly one message and it was sent by the driver, not the rider. Limb (c) fails affirmatively on admissible fixes: there are zero qualifying rider fixes (rider_qualifying_fix_count = 0) and the rider's device sat between 797.9 m and 804.8 m from the pickup pin throughout — roughly eight times the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius.

The chat log corroborates the driver's account: at 21:26:42, within twenty seconds of the arrival marker, the driver wrote 'im at the pickup point', delivered at 21:26:43 and read by the rider at 21:27:12. The rider never replied before the driver terminated the trip at 21:33:39, and the counterparty statement on file says 'Rider did not show after the waiting period.' The driver did everything the no-show process asks of him.

POL-NS-03 does not apply and yields no refund route. That clause governs stationary fixes OUTSIDE the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's stationary fixes are inside the 50 m STANDARD radius (minimum distance 0.11 m), so the wrong-entrance band is never entered. Independently, registered_pickup_points is 1, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill of POL-NS-03(ii) — which requires 2 or more registered points — could not arise on these facts either.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip, so compensation is paid rather than withheld. It requires BOTH limbs: no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more AND that count divided by completed_trips_30d greater than 0.08. The driver's trailing-30-day no-show terminations stand at 3 (below 4) and 3 divided by 40 completed trips is 0.075 (not greater than 0.08). This is the only profile test the clause permits, and it is passed.

The driver's payout is SGD 3.60 — 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee in force for this trip, with the residual 20 percent retained as the platform service fee. That is the net figure the platform's own money block computes from POL-NS-07 (driver_compensation '3.60'), and it is deliberately not the rider's gross figure of SGD 6.61.

The ruling on this case is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, not a bare NO_ACTION. POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full on limbs (a) through (d), no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-07 therefore fixes the driver's payout and requires the emitted ruling value to be DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd. The rider's charge of SGD 4.50 stands as it presently is (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) with no refund.

No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is engaged. Counterparty dispute history is zero on both sides, so limb (c) cannot fire; the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so limb (d) cannot fire; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip, so the other half of limb (d) cannot fire; and there is no direct contradiction between artifacts, since the platform's arrival event and the GPS first in-geofence fix agree to the second and the fare line reconciles exactly to the net fee. The automated pipeline can decide this case.

Nothing in this bundle is impaired, so no claim of mine is discounted. Every artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: the GPS trace has 100.0 percent coverage, a 10 second cadence, an empty gaps list and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so POL-NS-08(b) is not engaged; the chat log's single message matches the trip record's chat_message_count of 1 and its msg_id sequence is intact, so POL-NS-08(c) is not engaged; and the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line of 4.50 equals the net amount produced for this trip, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. The arrival event matched to a GPS fix carries no clock skew beyond 90 seconds — it matches to the second.

The one MISSING artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02728-01, is disclosed as impaired: it carries status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, and its payload is absent. The driver does not rely on it, and does not need to: the advisory matters only to POL-NS-06(i), which permits separated in-geofence intervals to be summed. Here there is a single unbroken 436 second run inside the radius (run_count = 1), so no accumulation and no advisory is required. The absence is citable but neutral — it neither excuses a shortfall nor creates one.

For completeness on the money: the waiting-time line on this trip is 0.00, so nothing was double-charged, and the only amount on the ledger is the 4.50 cancellation fee that POL-NS-01 makes chargeable and POL-NS-07 splits 80/20 in the driver's favour. The rider's $4.50 was the consideration for a driver who arrived, waited 436 seconds and messaged the rider; it is not refundable and it is not the platform's to keep alone.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your $4.50 no-show cancellation fee stands. To the driver: you are paid $3.60 of it, with $0.90 retained by the platform.

The driver's arrival and wait are documented end to end. The trip record shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 21:26:22, and the GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius at that same second (closest fix 0.11 m from the pin). He then held position there without a break for 436 seconds — 45 qualifying in-radius fixes from 21:26:22 to 21:33:38 — against the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). He terminated the trip at 21:33:39 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one second after that dwell completed. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 therefore hold.

None of the refund routes opens. POL-NS-06 (waiting-period shortfall) fails on arithmetic: the effective in-geofence dwell exceeds the 180 s minimum by 256 seconds, a surplus and not a shortfall. POL-NS-05 (false arrival marker) does not bite: the first qualifying in-geofence fix coincides with the arrival tap (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), so no waiting clock is recomputed and no false-arrival referral arises. POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance) does not apply: the driver's stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius, not in the band beyond it, and the record carries a single registered pickup point, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill could not arise either. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: the chat log's only message was sent by the driver ('im at the pickup point', 21:26:42, read 21:27:12), not by the rider, so limb (a) fails, and the rider's track sits roughly 798 m from the pin throughout — far outside the 100 m rider-presence radius — so limb (c) does not hold either. We record the rider's distance as context only and make no separate adverse finding about the rider from it: no clause makes rider position an element of the charge, and the rider is right that it is not one.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02728-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT). It is not relied on by either side: the dwell is a single unbroken 436-second run, so POL-NS-06(i)'s accumulation rule is never needed, and no advisory is required to excuse anything. Its absence is citable but neutral.

On the money, POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the fee in force under POL-NS-01, i.e. $3.60 of the $4.50, with the residual $0.90 retained as the platform service fee; that is the platform's net figure, and the rider's gross figure of $6.61 is deliberately not the payout base. The anti-farming check does not trip: the driver's trailing-30-day no-show terminations are 3, below the absolute limb of 4, and 3 divided by 40 completed trips is 0.075, not greater than 0.08, so compensation is paid rather than withheld. Accordingly the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and amount_sgd carries the same figure as driver_compensation_sgd ($3.60) — it is the amount this ruling moves, not a second payment and not a refund to the rider. The waiting-time line is $0.00, so nothing is double-charged.

No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is engaged: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the artifacts agree (the arrival event and the first in-geofence fix match to the second, and the fare line reconciles exactly), and neither the counterparty-dispute counter nor the rider's 30-day no-show dispute counter reaches its threshold. The monetary effect of $3.60 is below the $8.00 execution threshold, so the ruling issues and executes automatically. No referral is produced: POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire because the arrival marker is true, and POL-NS-03 does not apply. The dispute is decided on the driver's arrival and dwell evidence, both at full weight (1.0), and no artifact relied on is impaired.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
